title: Will this box fit the shelf?
hook: The label says 40 cm wide. The shelf opening is 42 cm.

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: The external envelope includes protrusions. Adding two handles to the body width changes the fit test even though the advertised box-body dimensions stay the same.

misconception: The two pictured methods are interchangeable without checking their mechanism or constraints.
objective: The external envelope includes protrusions. Adding two handles to the body width changes the fit test even though the advertised box-body dimensions stay the same.

claims.text: Scenario and prediction: The label says 40 cm wide. The shelf opening is 42 cm. Does this box, as drawn, fit the 42 cm opening? Correct option: No, it is too wide (40 + 2 × 3 = 46 cm against a 42 cm opening).
claims.source: home-models.ts case 'clearance'; values [40, 3], initial 42. Content patch r9 batch D (cm-lifehacks, company/reviews/lifehacks-200/content-patch-r9-batch-d.md block 1), applied by demo-builder for W-608 (2026-10-14).
claims.note: FC W-740 (2026-10-14): 40 + 2 × 3 = 46 cm > 42 cm; clearance 42 - 46 = -4 cm. The v2 drawing shows both handles at predict on one 4 px/cm scale, so "as drawn" holds.

recall.question: A box body is 38 cm wide, with a 4 cm handle sticking out on each side. What width must the shelf opening exceed?
recall.why: The outer envelope includes both handles: 38 + 2 × 4 = 46 cm. The body width alone hides an 8 cm collision.
